To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the activity concentrations of the 210Pbl and 210Po radionuclids in the fly ash from the NID system were 3-4 times higher than in the ash from the ESP systems, which was mainly due to the higher efficiency of the NID system in collecting the ash from the outlet.

the activity concentration of the naturally occurring 210Pb, and 210Po radionuclids in fly ash from the two largest oil shale-fired PPS in Estonia, is up to 300 Bq/kg, which is 2 to 5 times higher compared to the values for coal-fired PPS in the EU.
the 210Pob and 210Po emissions have been significantly reduced in the last decades, but the emissions remain still relatively high.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the environmental impact of the world's oldest large-scale oil shale industry.
the environmental impact of oil shale-fired PPS, which are among the most polluting energy production facilities worldwide.
the environmental impact of 210Pobased radionuclids emitted from oil shale-fired Pps.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the implementation of higher efficiency purification systems has significantly reduced negative effects of the oil shale-fired PPS on the environment.
the modernized Estonian oil shale-fired PPS are among the most advanced power plants in the world with regard to environmental emissions and the associated radiation exposure risks.
the 210Po and 210Pb emissions from oil shale-fired PPS are low, with a significant reduction in recent decades, and the potential radiation exposure risk is very low.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 210Po and 210Pb atmospheric emissions from the modernized oil shale-fired PPS are not significant and do not represent a radiation hazard to humans or the environment.
the 210Pob and 210Po atmospheric releases from the modernized oil shale-fired power plant are significantly reduced compared to the situation 20-30 years ago.
the 210Po and 210Pb emissions from the modernized oil shale-fired PPS are significantly lower than those from coal-fired PPs and the emissions have decreased over time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the modernization and implementation of higher efficiency purification systems in oil shale-fired PPS has reduced the negative effect on the environment and human health.
the modernized PPS are no longer significant emitters of 210Pbl and 210Po.
modernized oil shale-fired power plant technologies have reduced the atmospheric emissions of 210Po and 210Pb to the environment.
